implementation: Python standard library only; no external services or packages
fixture_provenance: All example and test fixtures are explicitly labeled SYNTHETIC. They are not customer documents or external benchmark results.
scope: Strict JSON CLI accepting schema.fields and documents arrays
Configured field IDs, patterns, types and required booleans
Supported types: exact strings, integers, finite floating-point numbers, true/false booleans, valid ISO YYYY-MM-DD calendar dates
Exactly one named regex capture, (?P<value>...), per field
All matches retained; equal typed values grouped with their source evidence
Multiple distinct typed values reported as conflicts without selecting a winner
Missing required fields listed explicitly; no defaults or fabricated values
Invalid typed regex matches preserved as rejected_candidates with evidence and reason
Character spans use zero-based Python Unicode code-point indices with exclusive end offsets into the original, unmodified document text
Duplicate field IDs, document IDs and JSON keys rejected
Invalid schemas, unknown keys, invalid regex capture contracts, invalid types and nonstandard JSON constants rejected

Optional trusted synchronous extractor callback supplements regex matches and must return known fields, in-bounds integer offsets, and precisely typed values matching conversion of the exact source substring
Malformed or ungrounded callback output rejects the entire request
CLI prints one JSON result and exits 0, or a JSON error and exits 2 for handled input and extraction failures

api.callback_signature: extractor(document_copy, field_copies) -> list[{field_id, start, end, value}]
api.callback_grounding: value must have exactly the same Python type and value as conversion of document.text[start:end] using the declared field type
api.callback_number_type: float; an integer callback value is rejected for a number field
api.callback_date_type: str containing a valid YYYY-MM-DD date
api.multiprocessing: Regex compilation and matching run in a spawned process. Application entry points invoking extract must use the normal __main__ guard.

limits.regex_worker_behavior: Compilation and matching share the timeout, including process startup. Timed-out workers are terminated and joined. Limit failures abort the request, rather than returning partial results.

commands.observed: Printed valid JSON with quantity conflict [3, 4], missing purchase_order, one rejected invalid date, typed values and exact source spans.

limitations: Processes text already supplied as strings; no PDF parsing, OCR, tables, files beyond the JSON CLI input, or semantic document understanding.
Field correctness depends on configured regex context. Substring grounding establishes textual evidence, not semantic truth.
Regex finditer returns non-overlapping matches per pattern. A nonparticipating optional value group contributes no candidate.
No currency, locale, whitespace, fuzzy-name or free-form date normalization. Strings remain exact; numeric and boolean lexical forms are intentionally restricted.
Numbers use binary floating-point and can round; equal resulting typed values are merged. This is not an exact financial decimal implementation.
Injected callbacks are trusted local code, not sandboxed or time-limited. No callback is used by the CLI example.
The process timeout bounds regex work but is not an operating-system memory quota or a strict whole-request wall-clock deadline.
The CLI byte limit applies before JSON parsing. Direct Python callers are governed by the schema, document, pattern and candidate limits instead.
The 2-second regex worker budget can reject otherwise valid work on a heavily loaded or slow host.
Tests cover labeled synthetic cases only; no claim of customer accuracy or production deployment readiness.
